weekly_digest.narrative: 本周日均 140 条。合并 140 条、关闭 203 条。领域分布：推理 583、训练 311、方向 6、通用 77。热点主题：CUDA/Kernel (257)、GRPO/PPO (154)、Attention (138)。
weekly_digest.coverage_note: 快照覆盖不均：Megatron-LM、TensorRT-LLM、sglang、vllm 不足 7 天，总量与仓库排名仅供趋势参考

focus: vllm 与 sglang 本周围绕 PD 分离的持续 rollout 做 pause/resume 机制，让长任务在不阻塞调度器的情况下分阶段传输 KV，是推理吞吐提升的关键路径。
TensorRT-LLM 与 Megatron-LM 在 MoE 与量化上密集修复：NVLS 集正确性、NVFP4 NaN 静默转换、MXFP8 RoPE 融合，直接影响多卡训练稳定性与推理延迟。
sglang 调度器对 hybrid SWA 拒绝重试逻辑做优化，减少不必要的同步 KV-cache 查找，缓解内存压力下的调度抖动。
verl 推进 Rollout replica 不停训重启方案（RFC），为 RLHF/GRPO 长线训练提供故障隔离能力，降低一次失败重跑全批次的成本。

modules.name: Attention
modules.note: DFlash2 候选选择分数接入现有置信度规划器，支持可变量化的 compact verification，长上下文场景下推理速度提升。

modules.name: Quantization
modules.note: 修复 NVFP4 将 NaN expert 权重静默转成有限值的问题，避免 per-token routed MoE 推理时输出污染。

modules.name: MoE
modules.note: NVLS variable-count 集行偏移由 int32 改 int64，消除共享 buffer 溢出导致的读写错位，修复高危正确性问题。

modules.name: KV-Cache
modules.note: Engine 新增 request-level bidirectional attention span 支持并对接 prefix caching，离线与推理 token prompt 渲染均可复用前缀。

key_prs.why: request-level 双向注意力跨度直接决定 prefix cache 命中率与混合流量隔离策略，线上多租户部署风险最高需重点 review。
RoPE 与 MXFP8 融合省去冗余 swizzle，Blackwell 上 MLA 吞吐有望翻倍，但对 TE 版本与算子覆盖有隐性依赖。
NVLS MoE 行偏移 int32 溢出会引发跨 rank 读写混乱且难复现，int64 化后释放显存上限同时需评估 int64 集成的带宽开销。
hybrid SWA 只在 freed capacity 允许时才重试，大幅削减内存压力下的同步 KV-cache 查表，但需防极端拒绝导致的排队饥饿。

items.title: [CPU] Size CPU worker memory per worker under a shared cgroup limit
items.author: ardecode
items.summary: Two fixes to how sizes its memory when there is more than one worker or the CPU's NUMA id isn't a memory node: 1. Inside a memory-limited container, each local worker reserves × the whole cgroup limit, so N workers together reserve N times that fraction of the…
items.body:
## Overview

Two fixes to how `CPUWorker` sizes its memory when there is more than one worker or the CPU's NUMA id isn't a memory node:

1. Inside a memory-limited container, each local worker reserves `gpu_memory_utilization` × the whole cgroup limit, so N workers together reserve N times that fraction of the limit. This PR gives each local worker an equal share of the limit.
2. `__init__` falls back to a valid memory node when the CPU's group id isn't one (s390x book ids), but `determine_available_memory()` read the original id again. This PR keeps the node chosen in `__init__` and uses it

items.title: [Quantization] Prefer Humming over Marlin for block-scaled FP8 on SM86
items.author: jhss
items.summary: On SM86 GPUs (A10, A40, RTX 30 series), block-scaled FP8 checkpoints such as run weight-only, and picks Marlin for them. This PR makes pick Humming there. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

On SM86 GPUs (A10, A40, RTX 30 series), block-scaled FP8 checkpoints such as `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` run weight-only, and `--linear-backend auto` picks Marlin for them. This PR makes `auto` pick Humming there. It also closes two gaps in Humming's FP8 linear kernel that the new default would otherwise turn into crashes: partial scale blocks and the weight cache. Part of Phase 3 of #65560.

## Claims

- **Speed:** on an A40, Humming is faster than Marlin in all nine serving cases of each setup I measured.

    | Setup | Output tok/s | Median TPOT, Humming / Marlin | Median TTFT, Humming

items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Follow-up to #50559, which put every route's auth level in. Two places where the Python and Rust servers still disagreed: - Wrong method on an admin route. Python looked a level up only on a full route match, so a request with the wrong method fell to and got …
items.body:
Follow-up to #50559, which put every route's auth level in `python/sglang/srt/utils/auth_levels.json`. Two places where the Python and Rust servers still disagreed:

- **Wrong method on an admin route.** Python looked a level up only on a full route match, so a request with the wrong method fell to `NORMAL` and got 405 without a key check. The Rust server checks the key first (401 or 403). Python now resolves the route as Starlette's router does (first full match, else the first route matching the path but not the method) and checks the key at that route's level, so both servers refuse before

items.summary: Completing external KV-cache offloads currently calls for each acknowledgement. Each call shifts the remaining list entries, so draining a backlog incurs quadratic pointer-shifting work.

## Motivation

Completing external KV-cache offloads currently calls `pending_offloads.pop(0)` for each acknowledgement. Each call shifts the remaining list entries, so draining a backlog incurs quadratic pointer-shifting work. Use a deque to make removal of each completed entry constant-time.

This is a bounded CPU bookkeeping optimization. I have not established that large offload backlogs occur in production or that this change improves end-to-end serving performance.

`/rerun-test` runs NPU test files, and `--hw` picks the backends a file runs on.

- A file registered only with `register_npu_ci(...)` resolves to NPU. A file that also registers CUDA or CPU still runs there by default.

A listed backend the file does not register is noted in that file's command comment (`# base-b (npu is skipped)`); a file with no listed backend gets an error line. `--hw all` runs every backend the file registers and does not mention the others.

items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Don't cache a block that a mid-block prefill resume ran past
items.author: wzhao18
items.summary: Fixes Mamba prefix caching publishing blocks with truncated SSM states when a mid-block resume runs past the block boundary, preventing garbage outputs on subsequent shared-prefix requests.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes Mamba `align` prefix caching serving the wrong SSM state. A prefill that resumes from a partial hit inside a Mamba block and runs past that block's end leaves the block holding the **resume-point** state. `cache_blocks()` still publishes the block under its **full-block** hash, so the next request sharing that prefix gets a full-block hit, loads the truncated state and generates garbage.

Related: #53614 (lets a mid-block resume run past the block boundary when the backend exports the prompt checkpoint internally), #66938 (uses the same masking idea in a broader change).

items.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fail only the request when an adapter cannot be loaded
items.author: BitlyTwiser
items.summary: Moves LoRA adapter loading from execute_model to request admission time so loader failures kill only the failing request instead of the entire engine, and prevents eviction of in-use adapters.
items.body:
## Overview

A LoRA adapter that was evicted from the CPU cache is read from disk again inside `execute_model`. If that read fails, for example because the adapter's files are gone, the exception leaves the step and the engine dies, taking every in-flight request with it. This change loads the adapter when its request is admitted instead, so a failed load ends only that request, and it stops loads from evicting an adapter that a running request is using.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Stop starving a request that waits for a LoRA slot
items.author: BitlyTwiser
items.summary: Binds the wait time for LoRA adapter slots in the scheduler so requests cannot starve indefinitely when adapter demand exceeds max-loras.
items.body:
## Overview

With more LoRA adapters in demand than `--max-loras`, a request for an adapter without a slot can wait indefinitely: the scheduler skips it, then keeps admitting later requests for the adapters that already hold the slots, so under steady traffic those slots never free. This change bounds that wait.

items.author: mosafariuk
items.summary: Fixes vLLM incorrectly selecting bf16 dtype on Linux ARM CPUs without FEAT_BF16 hardware support, causing inference server hangs during model warmup.

## Overview

On a Linux Arm CPU without FEAT_BF16, `dtype="auto"` resolves a bf16 model to bf16, and startup then did not finish warmup in 16 minutes on a Neoverse N1. `CpuPlatform.supported_dtypes` now offers bf16 on Linux aarch64 only when torch reports the capability, as the macOS branch already does through `sysctl` (#24129, #51627), and prefers fp32 otherwise.

items.title: [Kernel] Avoid unused GPTQ reconstruction workspace
items.author: FireHorseAutumn
items.summary: allocates a full fp16 reconstruction buffer on every call, including fused Exllama calls that never read it. Allocate that buffer only on the reconstruct path. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`gptq_gemm` allocates a full `K x N` fp16 reconstruction buffer on every call, including fused Exllama calls that never read it. Allocate that buffer only on the reconstruct path.

Peak memory, not speed. At `K=N=4096` the dead buffer is 32 MiB: it inflates every call's peak, and under CUDA graph capture it is pinned for the capture's lifetime.

Related but distinct: #66914 changes kernel dispatch, not allocation. #60921 changes Exllama group-size correctness checks, not allocation.

## Claims

- Fused Exllama calls no longer allocate `temp_dq`.
- Reconstruct calls retain the same

## Overview

The DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 MTP drafter on ROCm runs `eh_proj`, a bf16 GEMM, once per draft step at M of 1-5 rows, where it is purely weight-bandwidth bound. It is declared as a plain `nn.Linear`, so it never reaches `dispatch_unquantized_gemm` and the `wvSplitK` skinny kernel that its sibling projections already use. This PR declares it as a `ReplicatedLinear(quant_config=None)`, which keeps the bf16 weight, its name and loading unchanged. Follow-up to #49791; same change as #53942 on the CUDA Kimi-K3 path.

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: Reduces unnecessary synchronous KV-cache lookups in the hybrid SWA scheduler by retrying memory-refused admissions only after freed capacity is confirmed, cutting scheduler thread overhead from 31.5% to 2.0%.
items.body:
## Motivation

For hybrid SWA models the scheduler clears `batch_is_full` at the start of every round (#24359), because running decodes free sliding-window rows mid-step. When a request was refused for full-attention KV instead, that churn cannot admit it, yet the queue head is re-matched every round until a request finishes.

With the external cache linker, every match is a synchronous storage lookup on the scheduler thread. On Inkling with a tight device KV budget, the same queued request was looked up up to ~1,000 times, and these lookups took ~31% of the TP0 scheduler thread.

items.title: [Performance]: DP prefill cadence: a capacity-bound rank prefills alone while its lockstep peers keep deferring
items.author: ZhimaoL
items.summary: A rank whose last prefill step left requests waiting stops deferring and prefills on every step. DP ranks step in lockstep through the MoE collectives, so that rank's mixed steps set the step time for every rank.
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

**Problem.** With `--prefill-schedule-interval N` on a data-parallel MoE engine, the cadence is aligned across ranks (`step_counter` is identical on every rank), but the saturation escape from #44558 is not. A rank whose last prefill step left requests waiting (`Scheduler.prefill_capacity_bound`) stops deferring and prefills on every step. DP ranks step in lockstep through the MoE collectives, so that rank's mixed steps set the step time for every rank. The other ranks keep their own waiting requests and started prompt chunks deferred until the next cadence

items.author: taking-lying-flat
items.summary: Each partial LSE already includes the sink, so merging the states counts it twice: - Expected: - Current: Here is real-key softmax mass, is the value-weighted numerator, and. This affects target verification with on non-sliding-window layers, including GPT-OSS…
items.body:
### Describe the bug

FA3/FA4 cascade attention passes the same learned `sinks` to both prefix and suffix attention. Each partial LSE already includes the sink, so merging the states counts it twice:

- Expected: `(Np + Ns) / (Zp + Zs + S)`
- Current: `(Np + Ns) / (Zp + Zs + 2*S)`

Here `Z` is real-key softmax mass, `N` is the value-weighted numerator, and `S = exp(sink)`.

items.title: [Perf] Enable cadence-aligned prefills for DEP
items.author: chaunceyjiang
items.summary: Defers prefill work on off-cadence steps in DP+EP serving to keep rank execution aligned, yielding +8% throughput and −16.7% TPOT.
items.body:
## Overview

In data-parallel expert-parallel (DP+EP) serving, ranks share MoE execution and advance in lockstep. A rank that continues prefill work on a throttled step can delay decode progress on its EP peers, including when its local queue is full or it has no local decode request.

When prefill throttling is active and both DP and EP are enabled, defer prefills on every off-cadence step. This keeps the prefill cadence aligned across ranks and lets peers make decode progress. items.author: abhijithneilabraham
items.summary: With expert parallelism (EP), each GPU receives all token rows. Only some routes use its local experts.
items.body:
## Problem

Muse Spark uses the local expert count to select the Marlin tile size. With expert parallelism (EP), each GPU receives all token rows. Only some routes use its local experts.

The current calculation overestimates the number of routes per expert. It can select a tile that is too large.

For 128 tokens, top-k 8, and 256 experts across eight GPUs:

| Calculation | Routes per expert | Selected tile rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Divide by 32 local experts | 32 | 48 |
| Divide by 256 total experts | 4 | 8 |

items.title: [Fix] [NPU] qwen3_5_mtp: Load mtp.fc with ReplicatedLinear to support w8a8 quantization
items.author: paopaofish
items.summary: Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 ships a quantized. built it with, so the fc stayed on the unquantized path and MTP accept length dropped to ~1.3.
items.body:
Related MeetUp task: hw_008615958372123_01

This PR supersedes #49790 (same fix, rebased onto current main, opened from this fork).

## Motivation
Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 ships a quantized `mtp.fc`. `qwen3_5_mtp.py` built it with `nn.Linear`, so the fc stayed on the unquantized path and MTP accept length dropped to ~1.3.

## Modifications
- Load `mtp.fc` with `ReplicatedLinear(quant_config=...)` so it follows the checkpoint quantization.
- Skip fc on idle forward batches.

## Accuracy and performance (4x910B3, TP=4, 128K input / 90% prefix cache + 1K output, c=32)
- GSM8K (200, 4-shot, greedy): 96.0%

items.title: [Bugfix] Launch reshape_and_cache_flash with at least one warp
items.author: MeKaustubh07
items.summary: Fixes a CUDA kernel hang in reshape_and_cache_flash when num_heads * head_size < 32 by clamping block size to at least 32 threads (one warp).
items.body:
## Overview

`reshape_and_cache_flash` hangs when `num_heads * head_size < 32` on the per-head path (HND layout or per-head scales). The symmetric launcher now uses at least one warp, as the asymmetric launcher already does.

## Claims

- Fix: no hang for tiny `num_heads * head_size` (e.g. 3 heads x 7 dims = 21 threads, as in the new test) with HND layout.
- New regression test `test_reshape_and_cache_flash_hnd_tiny_head`.
- No change for normal shapes: block size is unchanged whenever `num_heads * head_size >= 32`.

## Validation

Hardware: RTX 4050 Laptop (sm_89, 6 GB), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.

items.author: trtllm-agent
items.summary: pins FlashInfer 0.7.3, but the draft-front RMSNorm compatibility check does not include that version. With, the version check rejects the required fast path during initialization.
items.body:
## Description

With HiCache `write_back`, the device eviction walk backs its victims up to host and then blocks the scheduler on `Event.synchronize()` for those D2H copies before it demotes the victims. items.title: [Spec Decode] Per-position acceptance rate over the drafts that reached each position
items.author: LantaoJin
items.summary: Fixes per-position acceptance rate in speculative decoding to divide by drafted tokens per position instead of total drafts, correcting under-reported metrics under dynamic speculative decoding.
items.body:
## Overview

The per-position acceptance rate divides the accepted tokens at position `i` by the number of drafts. When drafts are shorter than `num_speculative_tokens`, for example under dynamic speculative decoding, that under-reports every later position, and a position no draft reached shows `0.000`. This PR divides by the drafted tokens at each position everywhere the rate is computed, and exports the counter that makes it computable from `/metrics`. A second commit seeds the dummy prompts of `vllm bench latency`, whose run-to-run variance hid this kind of change in A/B runs.

Follow-up
discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--67610.org.readthedocs.build/en/67610/

cc @tomasruizt since this follows up #64156 and mirrors its per-position verified counter. With dynamic SD on a real engine, positions 1–2 were reported about 6x low before this change (0.071 vs 0.451, see Validation).

### What does this PR do?

The torch backend of `FusedLinearForPPO` (the default fused backend) divides the bf16 logits by the temperature before upcasting to fp32, so log-probs differ from the rollout sampler’s formula (fp32 logits / T) by up to 0.054 at T=0.7, and the returned entropy is bf16. This upcasts first, then divides. No open PR or issue covers this.

items.author: hlin99
items.summary: Fixes improper async EPLB transfer thread shutdown by adding explicit stop/drain/join logic before Worker.cleanup proceeds.

The async EPLB transfer thread is started as a daemon, but has no explicit

returns. It can therefore remain blocked on `rearrange_event` or on a pending
layer result while worker cleanup proceeds.

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: commits text and advances / only when the new text is non-empty and does not end with U+FFFD. Some streams keep producing ids whose tail never completes, for example a run of lone UTF-8 lead bytes, or a run of special tokens that decode to nothing under.
items.body:
## Motivation

`DetokenizeState.step` commits text and advances `surr_offset`/`read_offset` only when the new text is non-empty and does not end with U+FFFD. Some streams keep producing ids whose tail never completes, for example a run of lone UTF-8 lead bytes, or a run of special tokens that decode to nothing under `skip_special_tokens`. In that case the offsets never move, so every row re-decodes the whole stalled window. Each row costs O(n), and the whole stream costs O(n^2). One such long stream can occupy the detokenizer process and delay every other request it serves.

## Motivation

A `/generate` video item object (`{"url": ..., "fps": ..., "max_frames": ..., "max_tokens_per_frame": ...}`) can carry two per-video budgets: `max_frames`, the most frames to sample from the video, and `max_tokens_per_frame`, the most tokens a sampled frame may use. A sparse checkpoint patch to a Muse Spark router weight re-applies `output_multiplier` to every element the patch leaves unchanged. This PR folds the multiplier into the incoming weight instead of the stored one. Same class of bug as #66944, in a loader that PR does not touch.

## Claims

- On main, a sparse patch that changes one element of a router weight rescales all the other elements by `output_multiplier` again, in both the NVIDIA and AMD model code. No error is raised and no NaN is stored.
- With this change only the patched elements are written, scaled once.

items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` rejects every connector whose `kv_cache_access` needs a single physical chunk, including `EXPORTS_FD`. The stated reason (UCX/RDMA cannot register driver-mapped memory) only applies to `REGISTERS`. This narrows the ROCm check to `REGISTERS`, so connectors that import the KV cache in another process through POSIX fds (e.g. `LMCacheMPConnector` in VMM mode) keep the extensible KV cache on ROCm instead of failing at startup.

items.title: [Quantization][RL] Buffered online quantization; direct reload of online-quantized layers
items.author: hao-aaron
items.summary: Online quantization loads each layer into a short-lived BF16 buffer and runs the layer's existing (PWAL) when its last shard arrives. Cold start and weight updates share that path.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Online quantization loads each layer into a short-lived BF16 buffer and runs the layer's existing `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) when its last shard arrives. Cold start and weight updates share that path. Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`) now supports online-quantized models, and online quantization no longer uses the layerwise reload machinery. Part of the direct weight reload RFC (#54477). This supersedes #65802 (same author), which staged online layers through the layerwise machinery, so it doesn't duplicate an open PR.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: The helpers in that set up a DP listener and a scheduler state their topology by overriding single fields of the active parallel context, for example. An override is validated together with whatever configuration is already published.

The helpers in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_shutdown.py` that set up a DP listener and a scheduler state their topology by overriding single fields of the active parallel context, for example `get_parallel().override(attn_dp_size=3)`.

An override is validated together with whatever configuration is already published. The tests therefore pass only when nothing is published in the process. items.title: [Bugfix][Compile] Key the AOT compile cache on loaded general plugins
items.author: arun-elr
items.summary: Fixes AOT compile cache reusing stale artifacts when general plugins are installed, by including loaded plugins in the cache key.
items.body:
## Overview

With AOT compile (the default from torch 2.10), a `vllm.general_plugins` plugin that patches code the model traces gets a stale compiled artifact when the cache was warmed without it. The plugin's change is silently missing from the model. This keys the compile cache on the loaded general plugins. Found while testing steering plugins in #36998.

## Claims

- A cache compiled without a graph-changing general plugin is no longer reused once the plugin is installed.
- No key change for deployments without general plugins.
- `vllm preload` daemons load general plugins like engine work

items.title: [Fix] [NPU] quantization: restore ModelSlim W4A8 MoE TP accuracy
items.author: OrangeRedeng
items.summary: ModelSlim W4A8 MoE initializes its scheme without a TP-size argument, leaving the default at 1. The down-projection compensation buffer consequently retains all 16 checkpoint partials on every TP rank.
items.body:
## Motivation

ModelSlim W4A8 MoE initializes its scheme without a TP-size argument, leaving the default at 1. The down-projection compensation buffer consequently retains all 16 checkpoint partials on every TP rank. Its per-channel metadata makes the loader copy those partials without rank slicing, so the subsequent TP reduction repeats compensation. In the historical A3 test this configuration produced 0/64 correct GSM8K answers, all truncated.

## Modifications

- Allocate compensation using the actual `layer.moe_tp_size`; reject partitions that cannot divide the checkpoint's 16 parti

items.body:
## Motivation

With DP (`--dp-size`) or DP attention (`--attn-dp-size`), each DP rank has its own radix cache, so a request only hits the cache if it lands on the rank that already served its prefix. The in-process `DataParallelController` never looks at the prompt: `auto` resolves to `round_robin`, and `total_requests` / `total_tokens` only look at load. So turns of the same multi-turn session land on arbitrary ranks, and each rank re-prefills the history. Under DP attention this hurts every rank, because the MoE layers run in lockstep and wait for the slowest rank's prefill.

items.title: [Fix] marlin: Load dense group scales and zero points at group boundaries
items.author: JonSnow1807
items.summary: With an FP8 block-quantized checkpoint, the dense Marlin kernel intermittently returns wrong GEMM results, which shows up as wrong greedy tokens. When a 128-wide group spans two 64-wide K tiles (M > 16), the kernel re-reads the group’s scale from its shared-me…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #45000. With an FP8 block-quantized checkpoint, the dense Marlin kernel intermittently returns wrong GEMM results, which shows up as wrong greedy tokens. When a 128-wide group spans two 64-wide K tiles (M > 16), the kernel re-reads the group’s scale from its shared-memory stage slot on the second tile, but warp 0’s next `cp.async` can already have refilled that slot with the scale two groups ahead, with no barrier in between. A lagging warp then scales a whole K tile with the wrong group’s scale. Both zero-point loads have the same pattern. vLLM fixed this in vllm-project/

items.title: fix(metrics): count each rollout once in raw reward mean
items.author: shx815
items.summary: When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards report a mean of.
items.body:
## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39971. On short prefills (B·NT·H ≤ 256), `chunk_kda_fwd` always takes the fused-diagonal path, which splits each diagonal block’s `exp2(g_i − g_j)` into two factors clamped to ±126. Without a gate lower bound, a channel can decay by more than 126 (log2) within 16 tokens, the factors stop cancelling, and keys that should be forgotten are read at near full weight. Error against an fp64 recurrence jumps from 3.0e-3 at a span of 125 to 0.116 at 126.

## Modifications

`fuse_diagonal` now also requires `safe_gate`, so ungated short prefills use the exact token-parallel diagona

items.body:
## Overview

The tiering manager looks up a request's prompt one chunk at a time, and for every chunk it records a query count, a hit count, and a sync-delay histogram sample. On a 128k-token prompt that is 8192 samples sent to the API server per request. This PR adds them up per request and reports one total per tier, when the request is scheduled or finishes. This also answers the evidence question from #60953.

## Claims

- Lookup on the scheduler thread: 5.7 ms to 3.3 ms for 8192 chunks.
- Stats sent to the API server per request: 74 KB to 540 bytes.

items.body:
Add OptimizerConfig.fused_main_grad_copy (--fused-main-grad-copy, default off). With it, _copy_model_grads_to_main_grads groups this rank's BF16/FP16 grad shards into runs of adjacent shards of one grad buffer (normally one per bucket shard) and converts each run with one vectorized Triton kernel (megatron/core/fusions/fused_float_upcast.py) instead of one .float() per parameter. Each main grad is a view of its run's FP32 tensor; the conversion is exact, so the values are bit-identical. FP32 grads and the precision-aware optimizer are unchanged, and the path works under CUDA graph capture.

items.author: AEGO-WRJ

items.body:
## Motivation

Setwise and multi-item scoring gather selected hidden-state rows into a contiguous tensor, split it into per-request views, then immediately concatenate the same views before applying the classification head. The concatenation allocates and copies a second complete pooled buffer. For 32 requests with 64 selected rows each and hidden size 4096, that extra buffer is 16 MiB in FP16 or 32 MiB in FP32.

## Modifications

Keep the gathered tensor and request counts together until after scoring. Apply the same head to the same two-dimensional rows, then split scores and, when requested

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: A rank's weight loader reads every checkpoint shard it needs through mmap. When the page cache is cold (a new node, or weights on network storage), all ranks wait on the same file reads.
items.body:
## Motivation

A rank's weight loader reads every checkpoint shard it needs through mmap. When the page cache is cold (a new node, or weights on network storage), all ranks wait on the same file reads. `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` already fixes this: each local rank prefetches a disjoint share of the shards into the page cache in background threads, so the node reads the checkpoint once, in parallel. It is off by default, so most launches never get it. The Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash cookbook recipes already turn it on.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: preserve the length stop reason in token outputs
items.author: yyDing1
items.summary: Today the vLLM rollout server reports both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work stil…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

### What does this PR do?

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units. These behaviors can drop adapters or export a nested `_flat_param`. An empty result then triggers a full-model CPU summon on every FSDP1 rank, defeating the memory bound requested by layered collection.

Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it
can keep that negative lookup cached for a while, so a writer on another node fails to find a directory that
already exists on the server.

_SafetensorShardWriter now calls mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) on every rank that writes shards. The call
goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

The SGLang patch stack adds TokenizerManager.post_process_weights, which always takes the writer side of
model_update_lock. During an in-place pause_generation the requests in flight keep the reader side, so the call
waits for requests that cannot finish while the engine is paused, and the weight update hangs. SGLang's own update
calls avoid this: update_weights_from_disk skips the writer lock while paused, and begin_weight_update and
end_weight_update go through _weight_update_session_call, which does the same. slime pauses the engines in place
whenever a weight update does not flush the cach

Megatron builds the state dict a checkpoint is loaded into with generate_state_dict, the function that also
builds the one it saves, and that function leaves out the optimizer and the LR scheduler whenever the current

therefore asks Megatron to load optimizer state it has no template for. With Megatron 4b4acac9a the

items.title: [#22150][fix] Register RPC response futures before sending requests
items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: A regular RPC reply can reach while is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22150.

A regular RPC reply can reach `_handle_regular_response` while `_call_async` is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout. Remote errors can be lost in the same way.

Register the future under the existing admission/close lock before sending. Include the send in the existing `try/finally` so send failures and caller cancellation remove the registration. Fire-and-forget calls still send without allocating a response

The sm_103 router GEMM runs ceil(rows / 128) row tiles of the next power
of two of the call's rows (8..128) each. A call whose rows sit just

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

Kimi-K3.1 has 96 MLA attention heads. Neither fused DSA sparse-attention backend took that head count, so DSA fell back to the dense PyTorch reference, which materializes the `q @ k^T` score matrix (about 192 GiB per rank for a 64K sequence at CP=8) and runs out of memory. This PR makes both backends serve 96 heads and fixes an indexer bug on the cuDNN backend that the same model reaches.

items.body:
## Description

In expert-parallel decode, every MoE layer waits for the GPU that receives the most routed rows. Experts are chosen unevenly, so the busiest GPU sets the step time, and the existing EPLB modes fit decode with CUDA graphs poorly. Online EPLB keeps a host copy of every expert and refreshes a few layers per iteration from decayed statistics; per-layer dynamic EPLB re-plans every layer on every forward and runs without CUDA graphs. items.body:
## Description

In decode, MegaMoE CuteDSL routed and computed the rows of CUDA graph padding requests and of attention-DP placeholder requests like real ones. Their inputs are identical, so they all pick the same few experts and load the ranks that hold them; late in a decode, when most requests have finished, almost all rows are padding. This PR drops those rows inside the MegaMoE kernels; it affects MegaMoE CuteDSL with CUDA graphs or attention DP. On 32 GB300 GPUs (DeepSeek-V4-Pro NVFP4 with MTP, EP32, one-shot decode) the late part of the decode is 37 % / 47 % shorter at 64 / 128 requests

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python

payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

## Summary

Implements the minimal full-disk weight refresh and weight-check interfaces discussed in #11.

### Full-disk weight refresh

- Add `POST /pull_weights`.
- Copy `source_dir/weight_v<version>` into the rollout-local checkpoint directory through a staging directory.
- Replace the previous local checkpoint only after the copy completes.
- Return the applied checkpoint version and local checkpoint path.
- Keep the receiver intentionally small: the VIME client supplies `source_dir`, `local_checkpoint_dir`, and `target_version`.

- sync default WORLD process-group reload support from THUDM/slime#2208 while preserving Vime's low-level memory checks
- fix the stale `SLIME_TEST_ENABLE_EVAL` consumer, register the process-group regression test in CPU CI, and install its explicit `psutil` dependency
- restore the ROCm NVML guard that was missing from Vime
- document the actual state of the incomplete disk-pull migration instead of referring to the nonexistent `vllm.srt` module
